t: Claims expenses that cannot be attributed to any individual claim, such as salaries of the claims department, are classified as:
o: Unallocated loss adjustment expenses (ULAE)
Allocated loss adjustment expenses (ALAE)
Acquisition expenses
Reinsurance costs
e: ULAE are departmental overheads spread across claims; ALAE such as survey fees are tied to specific claims.

t: The claims function is often called a 'cost centre' of a general insurer because:
o: Claims and claims-related expenses form the largest outgo and their control directly determines underwriting profit
It generates the premium income of the insurer
It manages the investment portfolio
IRDAI charges fees on each claim settled
e: Claims typically consume 70–90% of premium; efficient claims management is therefore central to profitability.

t: A claims audit by an insurer's internal audit department is intended mainly to:
o: Fix the premium rates for the next year
Check compliance with claims procedures, authority limits and regulatory timelines and to detect leakage
Replace the surveyor's assessment of each claim
Approve payment of claims above ₹1 crore
e: Claims audits review files for process adherence, overpayment (leakage) and fraud indicators; they are a control, not an approval, mechanism.

t: 'Claims leakage' refers to:
o: Premium lost due to policy cancellations
Claims that are reported after the policy expires
The difference between what an insurer actually pays and what it should have paid had best practices been followed
Reinsurance recoveries that are written off
e: Leakage arises from overpayment, missed recoveries, poor fraud detection and process errors, and its measurement guides claims improvement.

t: A fire policy shows the premium cheque was dishonoured and never replaced before the fire. The insurer should:
o: Pay the claim and adjust the premium from the claim amount
Pay 75% of the loss as a non-standard claim
Pay the claim if the agent confirms the cheque was collected on time
Deny liability, since under Section 64VB no risk can be assumed unless the premium is received in advance
e: Section 64VB makes receipt of premium a condition precedent to the commencement of risk; a dishonoured cheque means no contract came into force.

t: 'Repudiation' of a claim means:
o: Payment of the claim under protest
Postponement of the claim pending documents
Reduction of the claim for underinsurance
The insurer's formal denial of liability under the policy, communicated with reasons
e: Repudiation is a final rejection of liability; delay, deductions or payment under protest do not amount to repudiation.

t: Which action is appropriate when a claim is received on a policy that has a reinsurance treaty cession?
o: Ask the reinsurer to appoint the surveyor and settle directly with the insured
Settle the claim and never inform the reinsurer
Wait for the reinsurer's written consent before registering the claim
Notify the reinsurer of the loss promptly as per the treaty's claims notification clause, especially for large or contentious claims
e: Treaties require timely notification of claims above a threshold and give the reinsurer a right to participate; the ceding insurer still handles the claim.

t: For a fire claim on a building, which document is useful in establishing the cause of the fire?
o: Fire brigade report
Bill of lading
Bank statement of the insured
Driving licence of the owner
e: The fire brigade report records the time of call, extent of fire and probable cause; the other documents are irrelevant to a fire loss.

t: A 'letter of subrogation' signed by the insured at the time of settlement:
o: Acknowledges that the insured has no further claims against anyone
Assigns the policy to a bank
Transfers to the insurer the insured's rights of recovery against third parties responsible for the loss
Authorises the surveyor to sell the salvage
e: Subrogation entitles the insurer to pursue recovery in the insured's name; the letter documents this right, which in any case arises on payment of an indemnity claim.

t: If an insurer fails to appoint a surveyor within the prescribed time, the policyholder may:
o: Appoint any person of his choice whose report binds the insurer
Deduct the delay period from the premium payable
Complain to the insurer's grievance cell and, if unresolved, to the Insurance Ombudsman or IRDAI through Bima Bharosa
Approach the reinsurer directly for settlement
e: Regulations give the insured a grievance route against delays; a self-appointed assessor has no statutory status, though the insured may engage one for his own purposes.

topic: Special Features in Claims (Motor, Marine and Miscellaneous)
t: Under Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019), the no-fault compensation payable for death in a motor accident is:
o: ₹2 lakh
₹5 lakh
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 164 fixes ₹5 lakh for death and ₹2.5 lakh for grievous hurt without proof of negligence; ₹2 lakh is the hit-and-run amount under Section 161.

t: A surveyor who delays the report submits an 'interim report'. The purpose of such a report is to:
o: Inform the insurer of the preliminary cause, estimated loss and reasons for delay so that reserves can be set and the insured kept informed
Enable the insurer to close the claim file
Replace the final survey report
Fix the final claim amount binding on the insurer
e: Interim reports keep the insurer and insured informed where the final assessment awaits documents or repairs; they are not substitutes for the final report.

t: Which of the following is NOT a factor a surveyor must consider while assessing a fire loss on stocks?
o: The value of salvage
Whether the sum insured is adequate to apply average
The insured's credit rating with its bankers
The quantity of stock at risk on the date of fire
e: Quantity at risk, salvage and adequacy of sum insured all affect the assessment; the insured's credit rating is irrelevant to indemnity.

t: A 'loss assessor' differs from a 'loss adjuster' in that:
o: A loss assessor is engaged by the insured to present the claim, while a loss adjuster is appointed by the insurer to assess it
There is no difference in practice
A loss assessor handles marine claims and a loss adjuster handles fire claims
A loss adjuster is a government official
e: Internationally, assessors act for policyholders and adjusters for insurers; in India the licensed 'surveyor and loss assessor' is normally appointed by the insurer.

t: Under an agreed value (valued) policy on a work of art insured for ₹25 lakh, a total loss by fire occurs. The market value on the day of loss is ₹18 lakh. The insurer pays:
o: ₹25 lakh less 20% depreciation
₹21.5 lakh, the average of the two values
₹25 lakh, since the agreed value is conclusive in the absence of fraud
₹18 lakh, being the actual market value
e: A valued policy fixes the measure of indemnity at inception; the insurer cannot reopen the valuation on a total loss unless fraud or gross overvaluation is shown.

t: The principle of subrogation does NOT apply to:
o: Personal accident and life policies, which are contracts of benefit and not of indemnity
Motor own-damage policies
Marine cargo policies
Fire policies on buildings
e: Subrogation is a corollary of indemnity, preventing the insured from recovering twice; benefit policies pay a fixed sum regardless of recovery from others.

t: A 'first loss' policy is one in which:
o: The insurer pays only total losses
The sum insured is deliberately less than the full value at risk and average is waived, the insurer paying losses up to that limit
The insured bears the first ₹10,000 of every claim
Only the first claim in the policy year is payable
e: First-loss cover (common in burglary) recognises that a total loss is improbable; premium is charged on the first-loss limit and average is not applied.

t: Under the condition of average, when the insured is found to be underinsured at the time of loss, the insured is treated as:
o: His own insurer for the uninsured proportion and bears that share of every partial loss
Entitled to a refund of premium
Liable to pay additional premium before the claim is settled
Fully covered because the loss is less than the sum insured
e: Average penalises underinsurance by scaling down the claim in the ratio of sum insured to value, even where the loss is within the sum insured.

t: A motor accident claim under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is decided by:
o: The Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal
The District Consumer Commission
The IRDAI
The Insurance Ombudsman
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). MACTs have exclusive jurisdiction over third-party compensation claims; appeals lie to the High Court.

t: Under the reinstatement value clause, if the insured does not commence reinstatement within the stipulated period (normally 12 months, unless extended), the claim is settled:
o: Not at all, the claim being forfeited
Only for 50% of the sum insured
On the indemnity (market value) basis, deducting depreciation
On the reinstatement basis nevertheless
e: Reinstatement basis is conditional on actual reinstatement; failing that, the insured gets the depreciated value only.

t: A surveyor assessing a fire loss on plant and machinery on a reinstatement value basis should allow:
o: The original cost of the machinery as per purchase invoice
The cost of replacement by new items of similar kind and capacity, plus reasonable installation costs, without deduction for depreciation
The written-down value as per the insured's balance sheet
The second-hand market price of similar used machinery
e: Reinstatement value means new replacement cost of similar machinery; book value or original cost are not the measure under this clause.

t: The insured's claim includes ₹2 lakh for 'architect's and consulting engineer's fees' incurred in reinstating a building damaged by fire. Under the Standard Fire and Special Perils Policy these are:
o: Admissible in full without any limit
Never admissible under a fire policy
Admissible as an in-built cover up to 3% of the claim amount; any excess requires a specific add-on
Admissible only if the architect is empanelled by IRDAI
e: SFSP includes architects', surveyors' and consulting engineers' fees up to 3% of the claim amount; higher amounts can be insured by add-on cover.

t: In a burglary claim, stocks worth ₹12 lakh are insured under a first-loss policy for ₹3 lakh. Stocks worth ₹4 lakh are stolen. The insurer pays:
o: ₹4 lakh, the full loss
₹3 lakh, the first-loss limit, without applying average
₹2 lakh, being 50% of the loss
₹1 lakh, after applying average
e: First-loss cover pays the loss up to the agreed limit with average waived; the loss of ₹4 lakh is therefore capped at ₹3 lakh.

topic: Special Features of Property Damage Claims
t: Under the Bharat Griha Raksha policy, the condition of underinsurance (average):
o: Does not apply at all, the policy paying the loss up to the sum insured even if the sum insured is less than the value at risk
Applies with a 15% waiver
Applies only to contents and not to the building
Applies fully as in the Standard Fire and Special Perils Policy
e: BGR completely waives underinsurance for home building and contents, a key consumer-friendly feature of the standard product.

t: A trader's stock destroyed by fire is being assessed. Opening stock ₹10 lakh, purchases ₹40 lakh, sales ₹45 lakh, gross profit 20% of sales. The estimated stock on the date of fire is:
o: ₹9 lakh
₹19 lakh
₹14 lakh
₹5 lakh
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Cost of goods sold = sales less GP = 45 − 9 = ₹36 lakh; stock = opening + purchases − COGS = 10 + 40 − 36 = ₹14 lakh, which is the method a surveyor uses when physical records are destroyed.

topic: Special Features of Property Damage Claims
t: In a fire loss of profits claim, 'increased cost of working' is admissible only to the extent that it:
o: Exceeds the sum insured on gross profit
Does not exceed the amount of gross profit that would have been lost but for the expenditure
Is approved by the insured's auditors
Is incurred after the indemnity period
e: The economic limit test ensures the insurer pays only for expenditure that was economically justified in reducing the loss of gross profit.

topic: Special Features of Property Damage Claims
t: A 'material damage proviso' in a business interruption policy means that:
o: A BI claim is admissible only if the property damage that caused the interruption is covered under a material damage policy and liability under it is admitted
The BI sum insured cannot exceed the material damage sum insured
The surveyor must be a civil engineer
The BI claim is paid before the material damage claim
e: The proviso links BI cover to an admitted material damage claim, ensuring the physical loss was itself an insured event.

topic: Special Features of Property Damage Claims
t: A 'floater' fire policy on stocks is used when:
o: Stocks are carried on board ships
Stocks are stored in more than one location and the total value fluctuates between them, with one sum insured covering all locations
The insured wants to cover stocks against marine perils
Only one godown is used throughout the year
e: A floater provides a single sum insured across specified locations, charged at the highest applicable rate plus a loading.

topic: Special Features of Insurance of Persons
t: For a health insurance claim, which of the following expenses is typically NOT payable?
o: Pre-hospitalisation expenses within the policy period specified
ICU charges during an admitted hospitalisation
Day care cataract surgery
Cosmetic surgery undertaken for aesthetic reasons without medical necessity
e: Cosmetic procedures are a standard exclusion unless required following an accident or burns; the other items are standard inclusions.

topic: Special Features of Insurance of Persons
t: Under IRDAI health insurance norms, the maximum waiting period that can be imposed for pre-existing diseases is:
o: 48 months
12 months
36 months
24 months
e: The 2024 norms reduced the maximum PED waiting period from 48 to 36 months; specific-disease waiting periods are similarly capped at 36 months.

topic: Special Features of Insurance of Persons
t: A personal accident policy pays TTD at 1% of CSI per week subject to a maximum of ₹5,000 per week. An insured with a CSI of ₹8 lakh is totally disabled for 10 weeks. The benefit is:
e: 1% of ₹8 lakh = ₹8,000 per week, but the weekly cap limits it to ₹5,000; over 10 weeks the benefit is ₹50,000.

t: A workman aged 30 earning ₹20,000 per month dies in an accident arising out of employment. With the statutory wage ceiling of ₹15,000 and relevant factor 207.98, the compensation under the Employees' Compensation Act is:
e: Wages capped at ₹15,000; 50% = 7,500 × 207.98 = ₹15,59,850, which exceeds the ₹1,20,000 minimum and is payable to the dependants through the Commissioner.

t: A product liability policy covers the insured manufacturer against:
o: The cost of repairing or replacing the defective product itself
The cost of recalling the defective product from the market
Loss of profits due to a fall in sales after a defect becomes public
Legal liability for bodily injury or property damage to third parties caused by a defective product sold or supplied
e: Product liability responds to third-party injury or damage; recall costs and the cost of the product itself are excluded unless specially covered.

t: Under a liability policy, the insurer's consent is required before the insured:
o: Renews the policy
Pays the premium
Reports the incident to the police
Admits liability or makes any offer or settlement with the third-party claimant
e: Admission of liability without the insurer's consent breaches the policy condition and may prejudice the defence; the insurer controls the handling of the claim.

topic: Special Features in Claims (Motor, Marine and Miscellaneous)
t: Under the Marine Insurance Act, 1963, a 'constructive total loss' arises when:
o: The goods arrive at destination with minor damage
The vessel is delayed by more than 30 days
The insured value is less than the market value
The subject matter is reasonably abandoned because an actual total loss appears unavoidable or the cost of recovery and repair would exceed its value
e: CTL is a commercial total loss; the insured must give notice of abandonment to claim as for a total loss, otherwise only partial loss is recoverable.

topic: Special Features in Claims (Motor, Marine and Miscellaneous)
t: Under Section 161 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, compensation for death in a hit-and-run accident (where the vehicle cannot be identified) is currently:
o: ₹2 lakh
₹5 lakh
e: The Solatium scheme pays ₹2 lakh for death and ₹50,000 for grievous hurt in hit-and-run cases; ₹5 lakh is the no-fault amount under Section 164 where the vehicle is identified.

topic: Speed and Quality in Settlement of Claims
t: Which of the following is the best indicator of the QUALITY (as distinct from speed) of claims settlement?
o: Number of claims registered per month
Average TAT of five days
Low proportion of settled claims that are reopened or escalated to the Ombudsman or courts
Percentage of claims paid by NEFT
e: Quality is reflected in accuracy and fairness; a low rate of complaints, reopenings and adverse awards shows that settlements were right the first time.

t: IRDAI was constituted under the:
o: Insurance Act 1938
IRDA Act 1999
General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act 1972
LIC Act 1956
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The IRDA Act 1999 established the Authority; it began functioning in April 2000 and is headquartered in Hyderabad.

topic: Speed and Quality in Settlement of Claims
t: An insurer that treats small claims (say below ₹25,000) on a 'fast-track' basis would typically:
o: Refer each of them to a licensed surveyor for a full report
Settle them on the basis of the insured's documents and a desk assessment, without appointing an external surveyor
Reject them as uneconomical to process
Settle them only after approval of the reinsurer
e: Below the regulatory survey threshold an in-house assessment is permitted, allowing quick settlement at lower cost.

topic: Speed and Quality in Settlement of Claims
t: If a claim is not settled within the prescribed time because the claimant has not submitted a required document, the insurer should:
o: Pay the claim without the document
Write to the claimant specifying all the additional documents required at one time, rather than calling for them piecemeal
Close the claim as 'no claim' after 7 days
Charge the claimant interest for the delay
e: Regulations require insurers to call for all requirements at once; piecemeal demands are a recognised cause of delay and complaints.

t: The Insurance Ombudsman is required to pass an award within:
o: 30 days of receipt of the complaint
Six months of receipt of the complaint
One year of the date of loss
Three months of receipt of all requirements from the complainant
e: The Rules require an award within three months; the insurer must comply within 30 days of receiving the award and report compliance.

t: A 'Lok Adalat' is useful in claims disputes because:
o: It facilitates a compromise settlement between the insurer and the claimant, and its award is deemed a decree of a civil court with no appeal
It can impose punitive damages on the insurer
It replaces the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal
It hears only motor own-damage claims
e: Lok Adalats under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 are widely used to settle motor third-party claims by consent, reducing litigation backlog.

t: The integrated online grievance platform of IRDAI through which policyholders can lodge complaints against insurers is called:
o: Bima Vahak
Bima Sugam
Bima Bharosa
Bima Vistaar
e: Bima Bharosa (formerly IGMS) tracks complaints; Bima Sugam is the proposed insurance marketplace, Bima Vahak a distribution channel and Bima Vistaar a product.

t: The minimum paid-up equity capital required to start a life or general insurance company in India is:
o: ₹50 crore
₹100 crore
₹200 crore
₹500 crore
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹100 crore for a direct insurer; ₹200 crore for a reinsurer (Section 6 of the Insurance Act).

t: A 'staged accident' in motor insurance is an example of:
o: Application fraud at the proposal stage
Hard fraud, where the loss event itself is deliberately created
Internal fraud by employees
Soft fraud, where a genuine loss is exaggerated
e: Staging an accident fabricates the loss; exaggeration of a genuine loss is soft fraud, and misstatements at proposal are application fraud.

t: A 'Fraud Control Unit' (FCU) in an insurer is responsible for:
o: Investigating suspicious claims flagged by red-flag indicators and data analytics and coordinating with law enforcement where necessary
Approving all claims above ₹5 lakh
Conducting surveys for fire claims
Collecting outstanding premium from policyholders
e: The FCU is the specialist investigation arm envisaged by the fraud monitoring framework; it neither approves claims nor performs surveys.

t: 'IBNER' in claims reserving refers to:
o: Claims that have occurred but have not yet been reported
Future development (usually upward) in the cost of claims already reported, beyond the case reserves currently held
Claims that have been reported but rejected
Expenses of the claims department
e: IBNER (incurred but not enough reported) captures inadequacy of case estimates; IBNR covers unreported claims.

t: A general insurer has net earned premium of ₹500 crore and net incurred claims of ₹375 crore. Its net incurred claims ratio is:
e: Incurred claims ratio = 375/500 = 75%; a lower ratio indicates better claims experience relative to premium earned.

t: Data analytics and machine learning are used in claims management mainly to:
o: Replace the legal requirement of a surveyor's report
Score claims for fraud likelihood, triage them for fast-track or investigation and predict reserves
Determine the premium refund on cancellation
Issue licences to surveyors
e: Predictive models identify anomalies and prioritise handling; they support but do not replace the regulatory survey requirement.

t: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 is relevant to claims handling because:
o: It prescribes the time limit for claim settlement
It mandates the appointment of surveyors
Claims files contain personal data (medical reports, identity documents) that must be collected, processed and stored lawfully with appropriate safeguards
It fixes the interest payable on delayed claims
e: Insurers are data fiduciaries under the DPDP Act and must protect claimant data; settlement timelines and surveyor rules come from IRDAI regulations.
